documented: Management API personal access tokens are confidential account-privileged credentials; the provider demonstrates the sbp_ prefix.
Pinned Supabase CLI acceptance pattern requires sbp_ followed by 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters for non-OAuth tokens.
assumptions: CLI format acceptance is primary client-side specification evidence, not a server issuance or cryptographic validity guarantee.
Titus and TruffleHog candidate alphabets are broader than the provider CLI; the native PAT rule uses the provider constraint and imports neither digit-count nor entropy heuristics.
The separately prefixed sbp_oauth_ form accepted by the CLI is an OAuth credential, not included in this personal-access-token rule.
Native left word boundary and catalogRightBoundary prevent word-adjacent starts and partial acceptance before credential-alphabet suffixes.
evidence.fixture_method: Deterministic synthetic values authored independently from provider and scanner examples; no live credentials, randomness, external verification, attribute names or decoding. Positive variants exercise raw values, value-contained carriers and delimiters. Negative variants exercise public identifiers, malformed shapes, case and credential adjacency.

documented: Supabase documents sb_secret_ keys as elevated backend-only credentials which bypass Row Level Security, while sb_publishable_ keys are safe to expose.

assumptions: The 31-character alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen body is a conservative Titus v1.2.9 scanner constraint corroborated by the provider CLI example; the provider does not promise this as a complete hosted issuance grammar.
The native rule requires exact lowercase prefix spelling and catalog boundaries, without importing upstream case-insensitive prefixes, digit-count or entropy heuristics.
No project URL or separate field name is required; public project URLs and publishable keys alone are not secret candidates.

documented: Resend's create-key endpoint returns a confidential token separately from the API key's UUID identifier.
The documented response token has re_, eight alphanumeric characters, an underscore, and 24 alphanumeric characters.
assumptions: The eight- and 24-character component widths are conservative Titus v1.2.9 scanner constraints corroborated by a provider response example, not a complete or guaranteed issuance grammar.
Exact lowercase prefix spelling, native catalog boundaries and alphanumeric components are required; no digit-count or entropy heuristic is imported.

documented: Tailscale explicitly lists api, auth, client, scim and webhook key prefixes, states keys/secrets are case-sensitive, and includes all five credential classes in secret scanning.
An OAuth client has a distinct client ID and confidential client secret; the complete secret is needed to obtain an API access token.
The provider key-prefix example contains both an ID and a secret separated by a hyphen.
OAuth client secrets may be supplied directly as --auth-key values with URL-style options beginning with a question mark.
assumptions: The native rule uses TruffleHog v3.97.4's two nonempty alphanumeric/underscore component shape but restricts the type to the five provider-documented secret classes; this is a scanner constraint, not complete issuance grammar.
Provider docs do not promise fixed component widths. No fixed width, digit-count or entropy constraint is inferred from example strings or imported from Titus.
ID-only values, unknown types, legacy untyped tskey values and public node/machine keys are not claimed.
Native catalogRightBoundary prevents partial acceptance before additional credential-alphabet suffixes; token-internal signed wrappers are not claimed.
